title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.10). K is a field finitely generated over Q, with algebraic closure K̄. k is the algebraic closure of Q in K, and n = trdeg(K/Q). Spec K = η is written as the projective limit of a cofinal system of smooth, geometrically connected k-varieties U_i. Following M. Artin (SGA 4 XI), these can be taken to be 'elementary' varieties, i.e. towers of elementary fibrations in smooth affine curves. For each i the homotopy exact sequence (12) is 1 → π_i = π_1(Ū_i, η̄) → E_i = π_1(U_i, η̄) → Γ_{Q̄/k} → 1. These sequences form a projective system with constant quotient.

On this page Grothendieck makes three points.
(1) The kernels π_i are 'geometric' fundamental groups. By the comparison theorem (Riemann existence, SGA 1 XII), once an embedding K̄ ↪ C is chosen (inducing Q̄ ≅ the algebraic closure K̄_0 of Q in C), π_i ≅ π_1(U_i(C), η̄)^ (profinite completion). Here η̄ is now read as a common base point of the complex analytic spaces U_i(C).
(2) Passing to the limit, the fundamental exact sequence (8), 1 → Π_{K̄/K} → E_{K̄/K} = Gal(K̄/K) → Γ_{Q̄/k} → 1, is the projective limit of the sequences (12). In particular Π_{K̄/K} = Gal(K̄/KQ̄) ≅ lim_i π_i ≅ lim_i π_1(U_i(C))^.
(3) Artin's elementary fibrations give, in characteristic 0, short exact sequences 1 → π_1(fibre) → π_1(total space) → π_1(base) → 1. The fibre is an affine curve, whose profinite π_1 is free of finite rank. Hence each π_i is an iterated extension of n free profinite groups, with n = dim U_i = trdeg K/Q.

The next page draws the consequences:
- cd π_i = n and cd_ℓ E_i ≤ n+2 for ℓ odd, using cd_ℓ Γ_k ≤ 2 for a number field;
- by passage to the limit, cd Π_{K̄/K} ≤ n and cd_ℓ E_{K̄/K} ≤ n+2, with equality, giving a cohomological description of the absolute transcendence degree;
- 'Théorème 1': open subgroups of E_{K̄/K} and of Π_{K̄/K} have trivial centralizer.

Purpose: to set up the anabelian/Galois-theoretic study of Gal(K̄/K) for finitely generated K, the 'Longue Marche' programme. The geometric part is described as a limit of profinite completions of topological fundamental groups of K(π,1) complex varieties.
errors: Minor imprecision: 'tout π_i ... extension successive de n groupes profinis libres' with 'cd π_i = n' (next page) needs each fibre curve to have nontrivial π_1, i.e. not A^1. A free profinite group of rank 0 is trivial and lowers cd. This is presumably what the restriction to 'grandes' elementary varieties is meant to handle, and in any case cofinal choices exist. For the limit Π_{K̄/K} the equality cd = n is standard (Serre/Tate: cd of the function field of trdeg n over an algebraically closed field is n).

The parenthetical 'plongement de K̄ dans C (c'est-à-dire un iso Q̄ ≃ K̄_0)' is loose. An embedding of K̄ into C induces, but is not equivalent to, an identification of Q̄ with the algebraic closure of Q in C. This is harmless for the argument.

ideas.what: Absolute Galois group of a finitely generated field as projective limit of étale fundamental groups of a cofinal system of smooth models U_i
ideas.modern_name: Galois group of the generic point as limit of π_1 of open neighbourhoods (birational anabelian setup)
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 V/IX; Esquisse d'un programme; letter to Faltings (1983)

ideas.what: Geometric fundamental group π_1(Ū_i) computed transcendentally as profinite completion of π_1(U_i(C))
ideas.modern_name: Riemann existence / comparison theorem for étale π_1

ideas.what: Using Artin's elementary fibrations, π_i is an iterated extension of n finitely generated free profinite groups
ideas.modern_name: Artin good neighbourhoods; K(π,1) property; 'good' groups (polyfree)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exposé XI (Artin), within Grothendieck's seminar

ideas.what: Cohomological dimension: cd Π_{K̄/K} = n, cd_ℓ Gal(K̄/K) = n+2 (ℓ odd), i.e. a cohomological characterization of absolute transcendence degree (stated on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Cohomological dimension of function fields (Serre's Galois Cohomology; SGA 4 X)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful expository setup of standard facts: the limit description of Gal(K̄/K), comparison with topological π_1, Artin neighbourhoods as iterated extensions of free profinite groups, and cohomological dimension. All of it is well known and documented in SGA 1/4 and Serre. The anabelian 'Théorème 1' on trivial centralizers comes on the next page and is itself known (Neukirch/Ikeda/Pop-type results).
transcription_corrections: After 'limite projective des suites exactes d'homotopie' a reference '(12)' is probably intended; there is a gap before ', ce qui donne'.

'Π_{K̄/K}' in the displayed formula is the geometric Galois group (capital Pi), and the brace under π_1(Ū_i, η̄) is labelled π_i. In the second line the brace label sits under π_1(U_i(C), η̄)^∧, rendered as ^.

Left margin note (oblique, faint): roughly 'Cette interprétation [transcendante] vaut [aussi / non seulement] pour (12), [mais aussi pour] (13) [?] ... Q ... ext. de corps K/K_0'. K/K_0 is written large at the bottom of the margin; the reading is very uncertain.
The word written above 'groupes' in 'extension successive de n groupes' is an inserted 'n', consistent with the transcription.
